records.assistant: both (Claude and ChatGPT have their own step-by-step sections; Adobe also names Copilot, GitHub Copilot and Gemini, and says any assistant that supports the same open standard works)
records.what_adobe_says: A client's team can link Workfront to Claude or ChatGPT and then, by typing plain requests, find projects, tasks and issues and, if the Workfront administrator switches writing on, create, update or delete them. In Claude there is a ready-made Adobe Workfront connector in Claude's connector list (or it can be added by web address); in ChatGPT it is added by web address as a custom server. Each person signs in with their own Workfront login and the assistant can only do what that person is allowed to do. Reading is on by default, writing is off by default. One connection reaches one Workfront instance. A few newer approval tools (parallel review paths) and the feedback tool are marked by Adobe as Preview-only, but the connection itself carries no such label.

quotes.quote: The Adobe Workfront MCP server lets you work with your Workfront data through natural-language conversation in a supported AI agentic platform.
This article walks through the connection steps for: Claude ChatGPT
Find Adobe Workfront in the connector list.
Your Workfront instance must be enabled on Adobe Identity Management System (IMS).

Your Workfront administrator controls MCP server access for your Workfront instance through two toggles in System Preferences: Read-only MCP tools (enabled by default) and Write MCP tools (disabled by default).

If you use an enterprise version of an AI agentic platform, your administrator for that platform must enable the Adobe Workfront connector for your organization or give you custom URL access to connect to the Workfront MCP server.
You must be an owner in an enterprise Claude environment to perform this procedure.
Each connection ties an AI agentic platform to a single Workfront instance.
The AI agentic platform acts in Workfront using your Workfront account, access level, and object permissions. A tool only works if you have the corresponding access in Workfront.
The tools that appear in your AI agentic platform depend on your organization’s Workfront product entitlements.
The highlighted information on this page refers to functionality not yet generally available. It is available only in the Preview environment for all customers.
The Adobe Workfront MCP server lets you find, create, update, and manage Workfront items by asking an AI agentic platform in natural language.
Lets the Workfront MCP server perform create, update, and delete actions on Workfront data. This option is disabled by default.
The Workfront MCP server works with any AI agentic platform that supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
Currently, only Claude is supported for this tool.

records.what_adobe_says: This is real but it is a different thing from 'use Adobe inside ChatGPT'. A client who owns Workfront Fusion can build an automation in which one step sends text to their own OpenAI account and gets an answer, an image or a list of models back. Nobody opens ChatGPT; the work happens inside Fusion using the client's own OpenAI key. It is one of Fusion's many ready-made steps for outside services, so it does not put ChatGPT on the canvas as an outside system, and Fusion itself is not a product in the tool today.

other_leads: Adobe's Workfront page also gives step-by-step connection instructions for Microsoft Copilot (through Copilot Studio) and GitHub Copilot, and names Gemini as an example of another assistant that can connect by web address: https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/workfront/using/basics/workfront-mcp-server/configure-workfront-mcp-server

Workfront Fusion can also be used from Adobe's own Coworker (standalone and in a panel inside Fusion) with no set-up; and Adobe lists further assistants and tools for Fusion (Microsoft 365 Copilot, Cursor, VS Code, GitHub Copilot, Google Vertex AI Search, Glean, Writer AI Studio, Postman): https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/workfront-fusion/using/set-up-and-manage-fusion/use-fusion-mcp-server/configure-fusion-mcp-server

Workfront also supports custom-built assistants: sign-in for the client's own application, with the Workfront administrator adding its return address to an approved list in System Preferences: https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/workfront/using/administration-and-setup/manage-wf/security/configure-security-preferences

Workfront Work Agents: Adobe also offers an Adobe-built Work Agent powered by Coworker and a Project Coordinator, both marked Preview-only today, so not publishable under the step 86 rule: https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/workfront/using/administration-and-setup/set-up-wf/configure-system-defaults/configure-ai-collaborators
